clips.send: A friend who thinks giving without expecting anything back is pointless, because one farmer's good deed came back decades later as a cure that saved a prime minister's life - awe, hope.
clips.caption:
A poor Scottish farmer heard a boy screaming in a bog, dropped his tools, and pulled him out. The next day a nobleman showed up to pay him for saving his son's life.

The farmer said no. So the nobleman paid for the farmer's own son's education instead, all the way through medical school in London. That son became Sir Alexander Fleming, the man who discovered penicillin.

Years later the nobleman's son caught pneumonia. The medicine that saved him was penicillin. His name was Winston Churchill.
